canonical_statement: Sufficiently small, asymptotically flat vacuum initial data satisfying the Einstein constraint equations and the decay and regularity assumptions of Lindblad and Rodnianski give a global solution of the vacuum Einstein equations in wave coordinates; the resulting spacetime is future causally geodesically complete and approaches Minkowski spacetime.
domain_and_universes: A 3-dimensional initial hypersurface with Riemannian metric and second fundamental form, its 3+1-dimensional Lorentzian development, and weighted Sobolev smallness; exact function spaces, constants, regularity indices, and Lean universes remain open for the statement phase.
ordered_binders: vacuum initial data set (Sigma, g_bar, k)
asymptotically flat coordinate end and background Euclidean/Minkowski structures
regularity, decay, mass, and smallness parameters
hypotheses: the vacuum Hamiltonian and momentum constraint equations hold
the initial metric and second fundamental form have the source theorem's asymptotic form and weighted regularity
the source theorem's weighted initial-data norm is sufficiently small
conclusion: The reduced wave-coordinate evolution exists globally, solves the unreduced vacuum Einstein equations, is asymptotically Minkowskian, and its spacetime is future causally geodesically complete.
degenerate_cases: Exact Minkowski data are included as the zero-perturbation case. Large data, matter models, non-asymptotically-flat data, and past completeness are not asserted. The harmonic-coordinate reduction alone is not the theorem.
